key_insight: Spatial-TTT applies lightweight test-time training to streaming video so a model can continuously select, organize and retain spatial evidence on-the-fly, achieving long-term spatial understanding without relying on huge context windows or offline re-training.
problem_solved: How to maintain and update spatial information from unbounded video streams — i.e., which visual cues to keep, how to organize them spatially over time, and how to adapt representations online under limited memory and distribution shifts.
method: Streaming architecture with a spatially-indexed memory that stores compact spatial evidence and supports prioritized insertion/retrieval.
Online test-time training (TTT) loop that adapts representation weights using self-supervised spatial consistency losses on incoming frames.
Lightweight update and retention policies to bound compute/memory while preserving important long-term spatial cues for downstream tasks.
impact: Enables adaptive, robust spatial perception for long-running systems (robots, AR/VR, mapping) by reducing offline retraining and improving performance under environment shifts; practical for deployed streaming vision with limited resources.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: streaming frames → spatial memory → TTT loop → updated model & outputs
Timeline / memory-retention graphic showing which spatial cues are retained, forgotten, or updated over time
Performance chart: task accuracy (or localization/map quality) vs stream length comparing Spatial-TTT to baselines
Frame overlays / attention maps highlighting retained spatial evidence and where TTT made corrections
paper_title: Spatial-TTT: Streaming Visual-based Spatial Intelligence with Test-Time Training
paper_authors: Fangfu Liu, Diankun Wu, Jiawei Chi, Yimo Cai, Yi-Hsin Hung
